coin._readme: Rome's own debasement (DECIDED 2026-09-28, Corey: debasement is one of the downfalls of Rome). Silver share of Rome's everyday silver coin (the denarius, from 215 the antoninianus), authored estimates: about 78% under Antoninus Pius, cut for the plague and the Marcomannic Wars, about 50% under Septimius Severus, a collapse to a few percent under Gallienus and Claudius II. It times the share of Rome's decline that the history curves owe to the coin.

coin._readme: DECIDED 2026-09-28 (Corey): near half of Rome's economic decline comes from the coin, with ties to Governance (the army's pay, mutinies and usurpers). The coin's share of each domain's historical decline (AD 155 to the coin's low in 268, the plague's step left out) falls as the silver does. Sound coin kept by a surviving Governance institution spares Rome that share after you leave (scaled by sway); a debasement policy brings more of it.

stakes._readme: Stakes in institutions (DECIDED 2026-09-27, Corey): you start with a 1% member's share; 10% counts toward influence but gives no oversight; 25% gives a voice (priorities, policy, a plague response); 50% gives oversight and control (oversee, mentor, charter, endow, audit, invest). Cost per 1% = domain base × (1 + stake% / 4).

prices._readme: Price level (DECIDED 2026-09-28, Corey). Each year prices rise by the inflation rate set by coinage policy: Rome's historical practice debased the denarius slowly; a debasement policy speeds it up; sound coin stops it (each adjusted by your sway over Governance). Everything bought with gold scales with the price level; pay for work catches up only partly.

currency._readme: DECIDED 2026-09-28 (Corey): gold isn't debased; Rome's silver coin is. Everyday money is denarii (1 aureus = 25 denarii, the official rate in AD 155); gold aurei are a separate purse whose price in denarii rises with the price level (history's debasement unless your coinage policy changes it). Internally money is kept in units of AD 155 aurei, so every other tuning value keeps its scale; the console shows and takes denarii.

denariiPerUnit.ref: DECIDED 2026-09-28 (Corey: historical): 1 aureus = 25 denarii in AD 155

exchangeAttention.ref: DECIDED 2026-09-28 (Corey: exchanging is an action); PROPOSED P0-26: a trip to the money changers at the Forum

savings._readme: DECIDED 2026-09-28 (Corey): gold across the jump. The machine carries a small purse; beyond it, gold can be deposited with the banking house (a little interest, with the risk that the house fails or its head embezzles) or buried (no interest, with the risk that someone else finds it). Anything else left in hand is lost. The arrival's Discovery beat reveals what became of it.
